title: Edge Scout: Composite Latency & Network Health Index for Region Ranking with Variant Escrow
creator: Leah Chen
description:
Objective: Build a composite region health index (Edge Scout) that ranks POPs for incoming inference requests by combining latency quantiles (p50, p95) with network signals (packet loss, jitter, path flapping) and capacity escrow so the router can select both the preferred region and a ranked set of fallback model variants.

Background: Current region selection uses separate p50/p95 thresholds and simple network penalties. We observe oscillation during partial outages and poor fallback choices (heavy variants chosen under congestion). Edge Scout will produce a single score that encodes latency distribution, short-term stability, and available variant capacity, enabling: 1) more stable region ranking with hysteresis, 2) tier-aware routing where higher SLA customers prefer lower-latency regions, and 3) variant ranking so the router prefers lighter quantized variants when capacity is constrained.

Design summary:
- Inputs: rolling p50 and p95 (30s & 5m windows), EWMA packet loss (1m, 5m), jitter estimate, open connection ratio, instance drain signals, and variant capacity counts from the placement service.
- Scoring: normalize p50/p95 into z-scores against historical baselines per-POP, compute a weighted composite where p95 gets higher weight for tail-sensitive routes. Network penalty term uses EWMA packet loss and jitter to bump the composite. Apply a stability multiplier derived from anomaly detection (short-lived outliers are downweighted).
- Escrow: reserve a configurable percent of variant capacity (default 10%) per POP for critical tiers; escrow is reduced gracefully as POPs near saturation. Variant ranking sorts compatible model variants (full float -> int8 -> 4-bit quantized) by score = composite_score * variant_cost_penalty * compatibility_bonus.
- Hysteresis and decay: avoid rapid flip-flops by requiring score deltas > threshold and applying time-decay for promotions/demotions (configurable windows).
- Integration points: router-service (ranking hook), telemetry pipeline (new mbeans), console dashboard (per-route composite), rollout controller (canary/pinned routes).

Acceptance tests: unit tests for score math, synthetic traffic sim showing reduced flip rate, end-to-end experiments showing reduced 95th percentile latency for tiered customers and fewer failed fallbacks.

Notes: prioritize readability in scoring math, ship with operator knobs for weight tuning.

acceptance_criteria: Edge Scout scorer library produces deterministic scores for identical inputs with unit tests covering edge cases
Router-service uses scorer to rank POPs and preserves backward compatibility when scorer is toggled off
Staging experiment shows >=15% reduction in route flip rate and no regressions in P50/P95 for P0 routes
Console surfaces composite score and raw inputs for at least three representative routes
Fallback variant ranking prefers lower-cost quantized variants when POP capacity is limited and shows no quality regressions in evaluation harness
